MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  Special City Council Meeting
  December 21, 2020

Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting was
conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the City
Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public comments that
were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Special Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Goodell
at 12:04 p.m., on December 21, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on December 18, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

Staff Present:  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Acting Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel-Anticipated Litigation: Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Paragraph (4) of Subdivision (d) of California Government Code Section
  54956.9: One Case (Participation as Amici in an Amicus Brief in the Case Titled Cynthia

City Council Minutes  1  December 21, 2020
   Campbell et al. v. Don Barnes, in his Capacity as Sheriff of Orange County, CA (Case
  No. 30-2020-01141117-CU-WM-CXC) Immediate Release of Approximately 1800
  County Jail Prisoners

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 12:05 p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 12:18 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

OPEN SESSION

INVOCATION: Council Member Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Brenda Cooper, M.V.: Stated support for Orange County Sheriff Don Barnes’ opposition to
releasing prisoners.

NEW BUSINESS

1.  Report from Closed Session and City Council Consideration of, Vote Upon and
  Direction to the City Attorney as Regards Participation in Amicus Briefs in Support of
  Sheriff Barnes Opposition to Prisoner Release.

City Attorney Curley announced that the City Council addressed in Closed Session
the concept of the City participating as a named member of the Amicus Brief that is
being filed. He stated that the City is in support of Orange County Sheriff Barnes’
opposition of the release of prisoners. The case started with Barnes v. Campbell with
the allegations that keeping prisoners in the County jail in the capacity that they were
at is cruel and unusual and that they are more susceptible in that confined environment
during COVID-19 and have greater health risks. The trial court judge agreed with the
ACLU and ordered the Sheriff to release approximately between one and two thousand
current prisoners back into the community to relieve the risk of those still confined
in the jail. He noted that there are about 14 to 15 cities joining to oppose the release
order and to support the appeal of Sheriff Barnes. The detriment to the community
both health wise as well as potential disruption from bad activity outweighs the risks.
The Sheriff has identified that there is health management currently being conducted
in the county jail. City Attorney Curley asked the Council for direction to participate
as a member of the Amicus Brief group to prepare and file a brief that supports the
Sheriff’s efforts to not release the prisoners.

Motion made by Council Member Sachs, second ed by Council Member Bucknum, to
direct the City Attorney to have the City join in the Amicus Briefs in support of
Orange County Sheriff Barnes’ opposition of the release of prisoners.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  2  December 21, 2020
 AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 12:30 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, January 12, 2021, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of January 12, 2021
